reasons.vendor:
No EVE-NG template - sourced from GNS3's real nethsecurity.gns3a
(catalog-diff/gns3-catalog.md row 174), which is the one entry in this
whole group to give a real, specific disk_interface (scsi, not the
usual "n/a") - used directly.
reasons.emulator:
machine left at plain "pc" - qemu.py's own disk_bus heuristic already
auto-upgrades a bare "pc" to "q35" for scsi/sata/nvme buses, so setting
it explicitly here would be redundant with (and could silently diverge
from) that existing code path.
reasons.description: 58): reaches the real OpenWrt-style 'Please press Enter to activate this console' banner with br-lan/eth0/eth1 up - this fix depended on NPX-1167's own virtio-scsi controller fix below (this profile's disk_bus is scsi). Wave 38.12/NPX-1167.",

settings.description: Nethesis NethSecurity. Real image sourced 2026-09-17 from the project's own official S3 bucket (nethsecurity.ams3.digitaloceanspaces.com/stable/8.8.0/targets/x86/64/nethsecurity-8.8.0-x86-64-generic-squashfs-combined-efi.img.gz - found by reading NethSecurity's own public GitHub Actions build-image.yml, since its GitHub Releases page ships only a checksum file, not the image itself) - free/open-source, no vendor account needed. Live-boot-verified through netplex's real platform (rule #58): reaches the real OpenWrt-style 'Please press Enter to activate this console' banner with br-lan/eth0/eth1 up - this fix depended on NPX-1167's own virtio-scsi controller fix below (this profile's disk_bus is scsi). Wave 38.12/NPX-1167.
